Polygraphia VI (1518, [Oppenheim]) — Cipher tables

Source witness: Bayerische Staatsbibliothek (BSB) München, 2 P.lat. 545#Beibd.1. Editio princeps. Trithemius's posthumous first edition.

What you are looking at

The Polygraphia VI is Johannes Trithemius's exposition of substitution cipher technique, originally dedicated to Maximilian I in 1508. Each of the six books presents a different modus of enciphering plaintext as a sequence of Latin words. The basic mechanism is constant across modi:

  • The plaintext is broken into individual letters.
  • Each letter is replaced by a Latin word drawn from a substitution column (the alphabetum of cipher words).
  • For multi-column modi, the substitution rotates with the letter's position: position 1 uses column 1, position 2 uses column 2, and so on, returning to column 1 once the sequence exhausts.
  • The cipher words are chosen so that any ordinary plaintext produces a grammatical Latin sentence — invariably a devotional invocation. The ciphertext is thus undetectable: it reads as ordinary monastic prayer.

Worked example — Modus Primus, eight-column substitution

To encipher the eight-letter plaintext ABCDEFGH using Modus Primus (the first cipher of Liber Septimus / Clavis Polygraphiae, eight substitution columns):

pos plain col cipher-word
1 A C1 facti
2 B C2 Certe
3 C C3 timendum
4 D C4 continue
5 E C5 sempiternum
6 F C6 fabricatorem
7 G C7 supercaelestium
8 H C8 compassionem

The resulting ciphertext reads:

Facti certe timendum continue sempiternum fabricatorem supercaelestium compassionem.

"[We have] truly been made, [to be] continually feared the eternal fashioner of the heavenly ones, by compassion."

To an eavesdropper this is an ordinary Latin devotional sentence. Only the recipient who knows to take the n-th letter of the n-th word's enciphering column recovers the plaintext ABCDEFGH.

How to read the table files

The substitution columns from this work's source are rendered per chunk under translations/style-c-cipher-key/full/. This work contributes 64 cipher-key chunks; 63 parse cleanly into Style C tables and 1 fall back to a verbatim source rendering (see Honest limits below).

Each chunk file:

  • Identifies the source chunk (e.g. full_chunk_0025).
  • States the per-page-section detected patterns:
  • A — one entry per line (single substitution column, or several columns concatenated on one page).
  • B — two or three columns interleaved per line (a X a Y or a X a Y a Z), with optional trailing source line-numbers.
  • D — letter plus several numeric cipher values per line.
  • Renders an alphabet-down / columns-across markdown table aligned by Trithemius's 24-letter alphabet (a b c d e f g h i k l m n o p q r s t v x y z w, omitting j and u), plus an optional 25th zu / zv / tv slot for the v-ligature.

Honest limits

  • OCR scannos are preserved as-they-appear in cell values (e.g. Vtigiz for Vtique, fabricatosem for fabricatorem, pissislimum for piissimum). The v1 parser repairs positional OCR errors in the letter markers (long-s misread as f; 2v misread for zv; iv/lv for zv) but does not repair content — that is a translation-quality problem (handled by the GPT-5.5 audit pipeline), not a layout problem.
  • Dropped column markers: where a row had its column marker dropped by OCR (e.g. a misericordislima factorem instead of a misericordislima a factorem), the parser splits the value into N equal pieces when N matches the section's modal cells-per-row, and leaves the value merged otherwise.
  • Letter-marker repair via positional alignment: when a column is near-full (≥ 18 entries), each entry's letter marker is rewritten to its positional canonical alphabet slot. This catches the common long-s/f confusion (where row s was rendered as f by the OCR) but assumes the column traverses the alphabet sequentially from a.
  • Wide multi-alphabet tables: a subset of chunks (1 of 64 for this work) hold very wide octo-modus tables that the v1 parser cannot sub-split into individual columns. These fall back to a verbatim rendering of the source OCR, with a comment indicating the parser's limit.

Provenance

Auto-generated from the OCR'd source by scripts/render_style_cipher_key.py and scripts/build_cipher_book_intro.py. The OCR pipeline, manual chunk reclassification (Phase 0.5), and GPT-5.5 audit are documented in data/corpus/_PHASE_05_FINDINGS.md and METHODOLOGY_GPT_AUDIT.md. This Style C rendering is one of the four content-type rendering styles chosen for the crypto-occult cluster after the 2026-05-30 Phase 1 specimen review.

gnis et arduis ab unitate cauendũ, propterea qâdis scribendi modus propter ipsum facile posêt esse suspectus. Verũ quicũq naturalis sua uoluerit industria uti prudenter, ex nostris inueniet subtíliora, & quaenos nôsatis polita tradidimus, facile reddet meliora In orchematen uerali magna latêt arcana, qâsi quis propriae intelle xerit, plura numerorũ mysteria penetrabit. Nobis em nec têpus erat necratio hacuice omnia profundere in publicũ, sed nostro uo dicio satís fuerit qâ fecimus pro institutione illũ, quibus nostra olim placebût inuëta, ut modos habeât plures nô solũ occultescri bendi qâcũq uoluerint ad participes industriae absentes, sed mo du etiã unũ producêdi in plures meliores et subtíliores iuxta unũ uscuilũs capacitâtẽ intelligentiae. Itẽ cu orchemata nuerorũ satisf in locis suis sint aperta et manifesta simul et earũ tabulae expâ fae, nô fuit isthũc necessariũ semel dicta replicare, ne prolixitãs ní mia tediũ lectori generaret. Sed et p numerorũ figuras exemplũ ponere scribêdi secretiũ nô existimauũ necessariũ, cu nulla fit in modo sciendi difficultas, apud oẽ qui in uel mediocrũ uigent ingenio. Simili facilitate signa numeradi uetustissima quae reduximus in lucẽ poterũt intelligi et cõprehendũ, quibus numerorũ cognitio producitur in infinitũ. Quotiens eminorũ numero uirgũ la supraponitur, millenarius designatur. Nã X. decémilia. C. centum milia. M. mille milia. X. decies mille milia. C. centies mille milia. M. milies mille milia signicat, & ita consequenter quouũ et quantũcũnq progredi numerando uolueris sine termino.

Explicit polygraphiae clauís Ioannis Tritemij abbatis Paeapolitani, ad Maximilianũ Caesarem. Impres sum ductu Ioannis Haselberg de Aia bibliopolae, anno a Chrïstonato M. D. XVIII. Men. Iulio.
